chapters.title: Why This Book Can Help You
chapters.sourcePressure: Opening problem chapter: pitch success depends more on method than effort, and common detail-heavy pitches fail because the audience processes status, attention, and novelty before careful analysis.
chapters.coreMove: Diagnose the gap between hard preparation and live-room uptake before reaching for more facts.
chapters.commonMisread: Pitching is just confidence, charisma, or more rehearsal.

chapters.title: This Is Your Brain, This Is Your Brain During a Pitch
chapters.sourcePressure: Practical brain-model chapter: live audiences first filter for novelty, threat, simplicity, and relevance, so dense analytic material gets blocked before deeper reasoning starts.
chapters.coreMove: Translate dense pitch material into simple, novel, relevant cues that survive the first audience filter.
chapters.commonMisread: The lesson is to make everything emotional or dumb it down.

chapters.title: The STRONG Method
chapters.sourcePressure: Bridge chapter: the first two problem chapters become a controllable six-step operating sequence rather than a diagnosis with no method.
chapters.coreMove: Organize pitch control into the STRONG sequence and see how each move sets up the next.
chapters.commonMisread: STRONG is a mnemonic list of optional tips.

chapters.title: Setting and Owning the Frame
chapters.sourcePressure: First solution chapter: live pitches are shaped by competing social interpretations, and weak presenters lose by reacting, overexplaining, or accepting the other side's assumptions.
chapters.coreMove: Recognize a frame collision and calmly establish the interpretation before the facts are judged.
chapters.commonMisread: Frame control means acting superior or starting a power fight.

chapters.title: Telling the Story
chapters.sourcePressure: Story chapter: a pitch story transfers meaning quickly and guides attention without rambling, front-loading history, or replacing substance with autobiography.
chapters.coreMove: Compress the pitch into a sequence of change, stakes, and point so the room can follow without drowning in detail.
chapters.commonMisread: Storytelling means a long personal origin tale or entertainment break.

chapters.title: Revealing Intrigue and Building Novelty
chapters.sourcePressure: Intrigue chapter: novelty and surprise keep the audience mentally active when they sharpen curiosity and consequence without becoming confusion, theater, or empty hype.
chapters.coreMove: Pace revelation so curiosity stays alive and the room keeps trying to resolve the tension.
chapters.commonMisread: Intrigue is clickbait, mystery, or theatrical withholding.

chapters.title: Offering the Prize
chapters.sourcePressure: Prizing chapter: the presenter protects value by avoiding needy seller energy, qualifying fit, and showing that the opportunity has selective value rather than begging for approval.
chapters.coreMove: Present the offer as selective value and make the room qualify for fit instead of chasing its approval.
chapters.commonMisread: Prizing means pretending not to care or playing manipulative status games.

chapters.title: Nailing the Hookpoint
chapters.sourcePressure: Hookpoint chapter: after frame, story, intrigue, and prize have prepared the room, the pitch needs a concentrated peak where novelty, consequence, and desire converge.
chapters.coreMove: Land the concentrated moment where the room can feel why the offer matters now.
chapters.commonMisread: A hookpoint is a slogan, tagline, or clever headline.

chapters.title: Getting a Decision
chapters.sourcePressure: Decision chapter: interest and intrigue must become a concrete commitment, because vague enthusiasm is not a decision and needy overexplaining weakens timing.
chapters.coreMove: Convert live interest into a defined decision or next step before warmth turns into polite delay.
chapters.commonMisread: Getting a decision means using closing scripts or pressure tactics.

chapters.title: What the Perfect Pitch Looks Like
chapters.sourcePressure: Integration chapter: the full pitch works as a controlled sequence of frame, story, intrigue, prize, hookpoint, and decision, with brevity and pacing protecting each handoff.
chapters.coreMove: Run the full sequence with rhythm so no stage crowds out or weakens the next.
chapters.commonMisread: A perfect pitch is a memorized transcript or rigid universal script.

chapters.title: You Are Now One of the Best
chapters.sourcePressure: Closing benefit chapter: mastery means repeatable room control under pressure through disciplined sequence, judgment, and anti-neediness, not swagger or universal domination.
chapters.coreMove: Turn the method into repeatable self-command so confidence comes from disciplined control, not hope.
chapters.commonMisread: The finish is motivational swagger about becoming unbeatable.
